answer: The fable that cheap identities can simply be priced out is wrong; instead, let trust expire. Keep reputation like a slow-rotting cipher ledger: scores accrue only through months of observed deals with established peers and decay toward zero when idle. A farm of N fakes then needs N separate aging histories in wall-clock time — money scales, seasons do not — and keeping all N continuously active to outrun decay multiplies their observable behavior N-fold, offering every fresh move to our detectors like nectar.
